shots.purpose: Open on a skate blade pressing bare ice: a hard, frozen lake you can still glide across
shots.claim: ice is slippery because of a thin near-surface water layer, not standing water
shots.evidence: full-bleed plate: skate blade on a frozen-lake cross-section, faint water sheen under the running edge, no explanation given yet
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in so the blade-on-ice contact reads as the subject
shots.transition_reason: cut into the classic pressure answer

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment plate of a skate blade on a frozen ice cross-section with a faint water sheen at the contact

one_second.relationship: the blade meets bare ice and glides

shots.purpose: State the textbook claim: the skate's weight squeezes the ice into meltwater
shots.claim: the textbook explanation attributes ice slipperiness to pressure melting under the blade
shots.evidence: diagram card: blade above an ice slab, one heavy rust pressure arrow bearing down, droplets squeezed out beneath the contact
shots.motion_reason: near-static drift so the squeeze relationship is the motion

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram of a blade pressing an ice slab with a heavy pressure arrow and melt droplets

one_second.relationship: weight presses and the ice supposedly melts

shots.purpose: Reveal the scale mismatch: a whole skater's weight buys only a fraction of a degree of melting
shots.claim: a skater's pressure lowers ice's melting point by only a fraction of a degree, far too little to make the water film
shots.evidence: split card: left, one huge weight arrow; right, a single tiny droplet beside the melting point, dwarfed
shots.motion_reason: held framing; the size mismatch is the information
shots.transition_reason: cut to the real mechanism at the surface

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment split diagram: giant weight arrow on the left, one tiny melt droplet on the right

shots.purpose: Show the true mechanism: a quasi-liquid layer sits on the ice surface even below freezing
shots.claim: a quasi-liquid layer exists on the ice surface even below the melting point
shots.evidence: cross-section card: disordered water molecules as a thin loose band on top, ordered ice lattice hatched beneath, dashed boundary
shots.motion_reason: slow drift along the surface so the loose layer reads against the rigid lattice

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment cross-section: thin disordered water layer above an ordered ice lattice, dashed boundary

one_second.relationship: the surface carries its own water below freezing

shots.purpose: Show glide feeding the film: friction warmth thickens the water layer behind the moving blade
shots.claim: frictional heating during glide feeds the near-surface water film
shots.evidence: card: blade mid-glide with a rust heat glow at the contact and a widening water-film wedge trailing behind
shots.motion_reason: drift along the glide path so the heat trail is the motion

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment plate: gliding blade with heat glow at contact and a water-film wedge trailing behind

one_second.relationship: friction warms the contact and feeds the film

shots.purpose: Split the cold: a thicker film in mild cold lets the blade glide; a starved film in deep cold makes it bite
shots.claim: the quasi-liquid film thins as temperature falls, so blade behavior changes with cold
shots.evidence: split card: left panel with a generous sheen under the blade, right panel nearly dry with bite marks in the surface
shots.motion_reason: held framing; the film thickness contrast is the information

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment split: two ice panels under the same blade, wet sheen left, dry bite marks right

one_second.relationship: colder ice starves the film and the blade bites

shots.purpose: Land the argument on the opening blade at dusk: ice is already wet, and every glide renews the water
shots.claim: ice's slipperiness comes from the ever-present near-surface water film, renewed by pressure, friction and cold-dependent thickness
shots.evidence: dusk reprise of the hero plate: blade at rest on ice, one calm glossy water line through the contact
shots.motion_reason: slow pull-out, the frame settles as the argument does

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment-plate blade at rest on ice at dusk with a calm glossy water line, warm light

one_second.relationship: the ice was wet all along; the glide renews it
